main_body: Tall brick townhouse with a slate mansard roof, a flat roof deck, a dormer and a chimney. Below the roof are an orange cornice, three storeys of brick wall with stone-framed windows, a balcony and a green door.
top_band: Slate and grey-blue roof surface, rows 17-43 (roof deck L≈95 over slate L≈79-134), ending at the orange cornice edge at row 44
evidence: The column scan shows a tall roof band with slate scale texture and a dormer, rows 17-43. The orange cornice at row 44 (L≈149/115) is a distinct front-edge line, and a dark row at 46-47 acts as an eave shadow. Below it the brick front face runs from row 48 to the base. The roof reads as a real sloped top surface, comparable to the reference house roofs. Windows have stone surrounds with dark inner reveals, and the door and balcony are inset. The walls are a normal vertical south face, so the building is a correct 3/4 structure. The step between the roof deck and the slate is small, but the roof as a whole is clearly separated from the walls by the cornice.

style.evidence: Brick has about 4-5 tones with per-brick variation, and the slate shows scale rows with some texture. Windows and the cornice are shaded in several steps. Flat-fill coverage is only 2% and median colours per tile is 14, so density is on par with the references. Total distinct colours is 47 against 185 and 66 for the references, so the palette is thinner. 97% of the dark edge pixels are neutral (#1d1722-type near-black), against 7-9% for the references. That is the uniform sticker-style black outline around the silhouette, not the tinted dark-material outline Beodeul uses.
